author: Plutarch
citation_detail: Plutarch, Life of Antony (Plut. Ant.), c. 100-110 CE. Loeb Classical Library.
notes: Primary narrative source. Written ~130 years after Antony's death. Plutarch draws on lost earlier sources including memoirs and Augustan-era accounts. Some passages likely incorporate anti-Antonian propaganda. Downgraded from A to B_high per v2.5 hardening: not a contemporary source.

author: Appian of Alexandria
citation_detail: Appian, Civil Wars (Bella Civilia) Books 2-5, c. 150-160 CE. Loeb Classical Library.
notes: Detailed narrative of Roman civil wars from the Gracchi to Actium. Books 3-5 cover the Second Triumvirate and conflict with Octavian. Draws on sources hostile to Antony. Downgraded from A to B_high per v2.5 hardening: written ~180 years after events, draws on secondary traditions.

author: Cassius Dio
citation_detail: Cassius Dio, Roman History Books 41-51, c. 210-230 CE. Loeb Classical Library.
notes: Most complete continuous narrative of the period. Books 41-51 cover Caesar's civil war through Actium and Cleopatra's death. Heavily influenced by Augustan tradition. Downgraded from A to B_high per v2.5 hardening: written ~250 years after events.

author: Marcus Tullius Cicero
citation_detail: Cicero, Philippics (Orationes in M. Antonium), 44-43 BCE. Loeb Classical Library.
notes: Fourteen speeches delivered against Antony after Caesar's assassination. Contemporary hostile source by Antony's political enemy. Essential for 44-43 BCE period. Downgraded from A to A_candidate per v2.5 hardening: contemporary but highly polemical; specific section references need verification.

author: Gaius Julius Caesar
citation_detail: Caesar, Civil War (Commentarii de Bello Civili), c. 48-47 BCE. Loeb Classical Library.
notes: Caesar's first-person account of the civil war 49-48 BCE. Mentions Antony's role at Pharsalus and as tribune. Contemporary but self-serving. Downgraded from A to A_candidate per v2.5 hardening: self-serving memoir, limited coverage of Antony.

author: Suetonius
citation_detail: Suetonius, Divus Augustus (Life of Augustus), c. 119-121 CE. Loeb Classical Library.
notes: Biography of Augustus with coverage of the conflict with Antony. Draws on Augustan-era sources including Augustus' own memoirs. Downgraded from A to B_high per v2.5 hardening: not contemporary, draws on Augustan tradition.

author: Augustus
citation_detail: Augustus, Res Gestae Divi Augusti, c. 14 CE. Monumentum Ancyranum.
notes: Augustus' first-person funerary inscription listing his achievements. References the war against Antony and Cleopatra. Propaganda but contemporary. Downgraded from A to A_candidate per v2.5 hardening: contemporary but self-serving propaganda; does not name Antony directly.

author: Various
citation_detail: Roman Republican Coinage (RRC) 489-545, 43-30 BCE. Triumviral coinage and inscriptions.
notes: Coins issued by Antony and the triumvirs provide contemporary visual evidence. Includes legionary denarii (32-31 BCE) and Cleopatra portrait coins. Downgraded from A to A_candidate per v2.5 hardening: numismatic cataloguing needs specific RRC reference verification.

author: C.B.R. Pelling
title_en: Plutarch: Life of Antony (Cambridge Greek and Latin Classics)
citation_detail: Pelling, C.B.R. (1988). Plutarch: Life of Antony. Cambridge Greek and Latin Classics. Cambridge University Press.
notes: Definitive modern commentary on Plutarch's Life of Antony. Critical analysis of Plutarch's sources, biases, and historical accuracy.

author: Adrian Goldsworthy
citation_detail: Goldsworthy, Adrian (2010). Antony and Cleopatra. Yale University Press.
notes: Modern scholarly biography combining literary sources, archaeology, and military history. Strives to separate Augustan propaganda from historical fact.

author: Ronald Syme
citation_detail: Syme, Ronald (1939). The Roman Revolution. Oxford University Press.
notes: Foundational study of the transition from Republic to Principate. Influential analysis of Antony as a Caesarian leader. Classic but Augustan-skeptical perspective.
